title: Carve 0.2 table marks
description: The marks of a pipe table: how a row splits into cells, the cell prefix, the span marks, the alignment marks and the whole-table attributes.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

sequence.description: The parts of the prefix in order.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

followed_by.description: What may follow the `=` for it to be the header cell mark (C2-B-171). Sorted by code point.

otherwise.description: Followed by anything else, the `=` is the first character of the cell's text.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

span_marks.description: A cell that holds only the mark joins another cell. Spans resolve backward only. Sorted by the code point of the mark.

failed.description: A mark that joins nothing is an ordinary cell that holds the mark as text; its prefix applies as on any cell (C2-B-173).

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

blocked_by.description: Where the mark joins nothing. A group is the head, the body or the foot (C2-B-174).

joined_with.description: What stands between the text of the cell and the fragment.

reads.description: What a fragment reads of the cell syntax: nothing. No cell prefix, no span mark, no row attribute.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

continuation_fragment.description: Where each fragment of a continuation row goes. Span marks are read from the first line of the row.

alignment_marks.description: The marks that come first in the brace block of a cell prefix.

alignment.description: none: the mark sets no horizontal alignment.

only_before.description: The mark stands only directly before a vertical mark.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

vertical_marks.description: The marks that stand directly after an alignment mark in the brace block of a cell prefix.

after.description: The mark is read only as the character directly after an alignment mark; elsewhere it is no mark.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

name.description: The key on the attribute line of the table.

clauses.description: The clause ids of the six 0.2 documents that the row encodes. The row is normative together with these clauses.

report.description: The code that reports misuse. An id of lint-rules.json.

value.description: The shape of the value. count: decimal digits, and an empty value counts as one. alignment_list: comma-separated entries, each one of `entries` after its spaces are trimmed; one empty or other entry makes the whole value invalid. width_list: comma-separated entries, each a decimal number above 0 and at most 100 after its spaces are trimmed; one empty or other entry makes the whole value invalid. count_list: comma-separated counts, one per table body, checked together with the other body keys (C2-B-230). An invalid value has no effect and stays in `attrs`. flag: the key alone.

entries.description: The values an entry of an alignment_list takes.

sets.description: The tree field the value sets, as `node.field`.

written_to_html.description: False when the renderer writes no HTML attribute for the key, whether the table consumed it or kept it in `attrs`.
